findings.title: Core architectural principles are carried through
findings.description:
- **Production pipeline:** replays run producer-only `P6` rather than a benchmark-only prompt (D8).
- **Grading:** it uses the objective grader unchanged, with an empty hidden set (D10).
- **Reports:** slice cases get their own tables, as the architecture's "Grading slice cases" note requires (D17).
- **Reference:** it is a reference line and is never ranked (D17).
- **Judging:** the pairwise judge is not folded into the grade, and no composite is computed (D17).
- **Absent is not zero:** harness absences drop the case, and config absences forfeit (D15).
- **Over-size diffs:** they are excluded and counted, never truncated (D14). That is one of the two rules the architecture's "Diffs for the judge" note allows.
- **Test sets:** no slice tests are used as hidden tests (D5).
- **Judge pairing:** pairs are limited to sample-matched cross-config pairs plus each replay against the reference. That avoids the quadratic growth the architecture's Cost section warns about (D13).

findings.title: Statements about edits to 421, 424 and 425 contradict each other
findings.description:
- **The claim:** Technical Scope says "No edits to 424 or 425", because 424 already provides `CaseKindRunner.requalify` and 425 already provides `bootstrap_mean_interval`.
- **Contradicting lines:**
  - Line 451 says `tests/benchmark/` passes unchanged "except where D8 routes re-qualification and D17 extracts the interval". That implies the interval helper is not yet extracted.
  - D17 and Consumes say `bench_report` (425's module) "gains the per-kind grouping and the pairwise section".
  - Line 321 widens 424's `CaseDrop.reason`.
  - D8 says a slice case set "now plans instead of refusing (424 D5)". That is a change to 424's behaviour, or to its registry contract.
  - Whether `requalify` already exists on the seam is not settled. D8 says `SliceCaseRunner.requalify` "calls" it, but the wording does not say 424 defines it.
- **Why it matters:** Slices 424 and 425 are the providers on the other side of these integration points. They need an unambiguous statement of what 426 modifies and what it assumes already exists.
- **Fix:** Add one table of every touchpoint in 421, 424, 425, 177 and 422. For each, mark it as "consumed as-is" or "modified here (what, and why no provider change is needed)". Drop the "No edits" claim, or make it true.

findings.title: The judge cost bound is labelled an upper bound but can understate
findings.description:
- **The architecture requirement:** Design Goals say a run "states its upper bound in dollars before any dispatch". Cost says judging is estimated from observed costs, and that the stated bound includes overshoot.
- **The gap:** D16 multiplies every call by one figure, the largest observed `DiffJudgment` cost for the alias or `--judge-cost`. It then prints `at most $3.88`.
  - Judge prompts contain the task text, which can run to tens of KB (line 527), plus two diffs. The over-size limit allows prompts up to 400k characters.
  - A per-call figure observed on small cases, or typed in by the user on a first run, does not bound a call near the limit.
  - The final "one call of overshoot" is also priced at that same figure.
- **Fix:** The bound is printed after every pair prompt has been built, so each pair's prompt length is already known. Derive a cost-per-character rate from observed judgments, or from `--judge-cost` as a rate for a stated prompt size. Price each pair by its own length, and price the overshoot at the longest pair. Alternatively, print "estimate", not "at most".

findings.title: The judge command's own I/O paths have no failure-mode handling
findings.description:
- **Covered:** D15 and D16 cover failed judge calls. They are left unrecorded, logged at ERROR, retried on rerun and counted. They also cover a missing run cap and a `tip_sha` absent from `--repo`.
- **Not covered:** these new I/O paths in `diff_judge_runner` have no stated handling.
  - A `git diff start..tip` in the user's checkout that fails or times out for a reference or replay diff. This is different from a missing sha.
  - A failed sidecar write for a normalized diff.
  - A failed or truncated diff read.
  - A second `judge` run, or a `run` or `grade`, contending for `<id>.judge.lock`. The doc says only "same process lock" without naming wait, fail or timeout.
  - A store write failing after a call has been paid for.
- **Why it matters:** The project's Failure-Mode Enumeration rule says each failure must be explicit and observable. D6 enumerates these for the build side (git failures become `harness_error`), but nothing parallel exists for judging.
- **Fix:** Add a short list. A git failure for a case makes that case "not judged, ERROR log, counted as harness-failed, retried on rerun". A held lock makes the command refuse, naming the lock. Add one test asserting the log signal for the git-failure case.

findings.title: The design carries scope that can be cut or deferred
findings.description:
- **Restated dependency lists:** Prerequisites, Interfaces Required, "Consumes from Other Slices" and Technical Scope restate the same dependencies four times. Keep Prerequisites and the touchpoint table recommended in the first finding. Delete the rest.
- **Speculative "Provides":** `normalize` "for any consumer that shows implementation diffs" and slice cases "usable by 427 if planted defects are drawn from slice diffs" have no consumer today. Cut them. The `CfRegistration` and `judge_pair` provisions are real, because this slice uses them.
- **Unused record field:** `max_prompt_chars` is stored on every `DiffJudgment`. Nothing reads it, because the limit is already on `OverSizeCase` and in the report line.
- **Undescribed flag:** `--keep` on `slice-cases build` appears only in the CLI signature and is not described anywhere. Define it or cut it.
- **Effort estimate:** "Effort: 3/5" looks light for the work. It covers about 13 new modules, four record types, three cross-slice extractions, a live spike that can block the slice, a new judge runner, and report changes. If the effort number drives sequencing, re-estimate it.

findings.title: The reference is `tip_sha`, where the architecture says "landing commit"
findings.description: The architecture's Envisioned State says "the landing commit is the reference". D2 uses `tip_sha` and gives a sound reason: on a merge landing, `fork..after` includes unrelated target work. The deviation is justified and documented. The next architecture revision should say "slice branch tip".

findings.title: Lockfile and changelog filenames are hardcoded in a layer the doc keeps language-neutral
findings.description: The Component Structure says build and qualify reach the language only through the adapter. `diff_normalize.py` hardcodes `uv.lock`. That is acceptable under the Python-only scope, since the constants are defined once. A second language would need the lockfile name to move onto the adapter. Record that in the design as a known follow-up.

findings.title: The frontmatter `dependencies` list omits 403 and 177
findings.description: The body names 403 (`slice_ranges`) and 177 (judge core, `ReplaySandbox`) as hard prerequisites, but the frontmatter lists only `[421, 422, 424, 425]`. If tooling orders work from the frontmatter, the mismatch could hide a dependency.

structured_findings.summary: Core architectural principles are carried through
Statements about edits to 421, 424 and 425 contradict each other
The judge cost bound is labelled an upper bound but can understate
The judge command's own I/O paths have no failure-mode handling
The design carries scope that can be cut or deferred
The reference is `tip_sha`, where the architecture says "landing commit"
Lockfile and changelog filenames are hardcoded in a layer the doc keeps language-neutral
